paragraphs.source_en: The master asked Meitei offhandedly, “Do you know this man named Kaneda?” Meitei answered with perfect gravity, “I know him, of course I know him. Mr. Kaneda is a friend of my uncle’s; he even attended the garden party recently.” The master said, “Oh? And who is this uncle of yours?” “Baron Makiyama, naturally.” Meitei replied, still more solemnly. Before the master could say anything, Nose suddenly turned around and looked at Meitei. Meitei sat there unconcernedly in an Oshima pongee kimono, with an old imported chintz formal overgarment thrown over it. “Oh! So you are some relation of Lord Makiyama’s. I had no idea at all; how terribly rude of me. My husband is always saying how much kindness he has received from Lord Makiyama.” Nose at once switched to extremely polite language, and added a deep bow for good measure. Meitei laughed and said, “Oh no, not at all, ha, ha, ha...” The master stared at the two of them in silence, utterly taken aback. Nose continued, “My husband tells me that Lord Makiyama also took a great deal of trouble over my daughter’s marriage...” “Oh, did he?” At this remark from Nose, Meitei apparently felt he had gone a little too far, and his voice grew timid. Nose said, “The truth is that many families have asked to be connected with us, but we must consider our own standing; we cannot simply marry her off anywhere.” “Quite so!” Only then did Meitei relax. Nose then turned back toward the master and at once resumed a less polite tone. “It is about that very matter that I came to ask you. I hear that a man named Mizushima Kangetsu often comes here. What sort of person is he, really?” “What do you want with information about Kangetsu?” said the master in a displeased tone. Meitei was quick-witted enough to explain on her behalf: “I imagine she wishes to know something of Kangetsu’s character in connection with her daughter’s marriage.” Nose said, “If you could tell me, it would be most convenient.” The master said, “Then you mean to marry your daughter to Kangetsu.” Nose immediately snapped back at the master: “I never said I wanted to marry my daughter to him. There are plenty of other proposals, so it would be no great matter if she did not marry him.” The master instantly returned the blow: “In that case, there is no need to ask about Kangetsu.” Nose, too, assumed a somewhat quarrelsome air and said, “Still, there is no reason for you to hide anything, is there?” Sitting between the two sides, Meitei held his silver-stemmed pipe like a referee’s war fan and inwardly shouted, “Go on, go on, fight it out!” The master struck Nose squarely again: “Then did Kangetsu say that he absolutely had to marry your daughter?” “He did not exactly say he wanted to marry my daughter.” “Do you think, then, that he wishes to marry her?” The master plainly seemed to understand that with this sort of woman, a direct frontal attack was the only method. Nose said, “Matters have not gone quite so far, but Mr. Kangetsu would hardly be displeased, I should think.”

paragraphs.source_zh: 主人漫不经心地问迷亭道：“这个叫金田的人你认识吗？”迷亭一本正经地回答说：“认识，当然认识，金田先生是我伯父的朋友，最近他还出席过游园会呢。”主人道：“嘿，你的那个伯父是谁呀？”“牧山男爵呗。”迷亭更加认真地回答说。就在主人要说点什么之前，鼻子马上扭转身子，瞧着迷亭。迷亭穿的是大岛粗绢长袍，上罩旧时从外国输入的印花布礼装外褂，若无其事地坐在那里。“噢！您是牧山老爷的那个什么呀。您看我一点也不晓得，太失礼啦。我丈夫经常讲他受牧山老爷的许多照顾呢。”鼻子马上改用十分客气的词儿，而且还外加上深深的一礼。迷亭笑着说：“哪里，不客气，嘿、嘿……”主人一声不响，吃惊地看着这两个人。鼻子接着说道：“听我丈夫说，关于我女儿的亲事，也真让牧山老爷操了许多心哪……”“噢，是吗？”鼻子这么一说，迷亭觉得有点冒失了，声音发怯。鼻子说：“本来有许多人家都想和我们攀亲，可我们不能不考虑自家的身份，不能随便就许给一个什么人家啊。”“可不是！”迷亭这才放下心来。鼻子接着又面对主人，立刻改用不太客气的口吻说：“就是关于这个问题，我才想向你打听，听说有个叫水岛寒月的人，常到你这里来，他到底是个什么样的人呀？”“你打听寒月，是为了什么？”主人用不太高兴的口吻说。迷亭倒是蛮机灵，代为解释说：“大概是为了她令爱的亲事，想打听寒月君品行的吧。”鼻子说：“如果你能说说，那就再好不过了。”主人说：“那么说，你是想把令爱嫁给寒月喽。”鼻子立刻顶撞了主人一句：“我并没有说要把女儿嫁给他。还有许多家来求亲，不把女儿嫁给他也无所谓。”主人立刻回敬了一句：“既然那样，也就没有必要打听寒月的事喽。”鼻子也摆出有点要吵架的架势，说道：“不过，你也用不着隐瞒吧。”迷亭坐在双方之间，把他的银管烟袋当作“军配团扇”似的拿在手里，内心里在呐喊：“干呀，干呀，见个输赢吧！”主人又从正面给了鼻子一棒：“那么说，是寒月提出非要娶令爱不可的啰？”“他倒没有说要娶我女儿。”“是你心里认为他希望娶令爱的吗？”看来，主人心里分明知道，对于这样一个妇女，只有用这种硬碰硬的办法。鼻子说道：“虽然他还没有明白地提出来，不过，寒月先生恐怕也不会不愿意的吧。”
